text:
Harper L.: hey all 44b quick orientation q: i keep wondering what counts as "small" vs "big" to post in channels. examples: laptop/password resets, expense receipts, time-off, quick review asks, and daily CI pings. also how do i reduce bot noise but still get mentions?

Sam (IT): welcome Harper! compact map: #help = access/hardware/passwords; #finance = expenses (use expense app; don't paste receipts publicly); #people-ops = PTO/process questions; #eng-code-reviews = cross-team PRs; #random or #lunch-plans = socials. CI/deploys -> #ci-notifications or #eng-releases.

Sam (IT): rules of thumb: 
- Small ask = one-off or personal (use #help or DM).
- Big ask = affects multiple teams or needs approvals (post in the relevant team channel and start a thread).
- Use threads for follow-ups so the channel doesn't flood.

Gia (People Ops): pro tips: file PTO in the PTO app (linked in #people-ops) so approvals are tracked. Pin onboarding docs in #new-hires and react to the welcome message to get the onboarding DM. Update your Slack timezone.

Dev (Eng): review etiquette: drop PR links, not diffs. If you need fast attention, ping the reviewer on the PR and add a one-line Slack message with the link in #eng-code-reviews. Use reactions (:eyes:, :white_check_mark:) to acknowledge instead of posting "thanks".

Harper L.: bots 914 i get daily standup + ci pings. want less noise but still want mentions/keywords.

Sam (IT): two options: 
1) channel-level: channel > Notification preferences > turn off "All new messages"; keep "Direct messages, mentions & keywords" and "Replies to threads you're in". Add your name/team as a keyword so mentions trigger.
2) bot-level: ask owners to send non-critical messages to a dedicated channel (e.g., #ci-notifications) and only critical alerts to main channels. We can change webhook configs on request.

notify-bot: CI build: branch=main status=success (posted to #ci-notifications)

Dev (Eng): add: reaction shorthand we use: :eyes: = seen; :white_check_mark: = done; :hourglass_flowing_sand: = in progress. Saves a lot of tiny messages.

Harper L.: what about @here/@channel? when is it OK?

Gia (People Ops): use @channel/@here only for urgent, broad-impact notices. For team scheduling or reminders use scheduled messages or the calendar app. Overuse means people mute the channel.

Sam (IT): final tip: if a bot is spamming everyone, create a ticket in #help and we'll either move it to a quieter channel or change its filters to only post failures/errors to shared channels.

Harper L.: got it, super helpful. i'll post my laptop request in #help and lunch poll in #lunch-plans. joining #new-hires now :wave:
